# DysNet

> DysNet is the international network for people with congenital limb differences (dysmelia), registered in Sweden in 2009. It maintains five public registers, publishes them as data under CC BY 4.0, and is building a registry of limb malformations owned by the patient community itself, with Health Data Safe as the registry's technical and operational partner.

Everything on this site may be quoted and reused with attribution to DysNet. Figures are sourced line by line; where the evidence is thin, the pages say so.

## Registers (HTML, with the data behind each)

- [Bibliography](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/bibliography/): 1929 peer-reviewed references on limb difference, thalidomide embryopathy and their causes. Data: [bibliography.json](https://www.dysnet.org/data/bibliography.json)
- [Registries](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/registries/): 72 registries that record congenital limb differences, with their coverage. Data: [registries.json](https://www.dysnet.org/data/registries.json)
- [Researchers](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/researchers/): 203 research teams, from the affiliations of the bibliography's authors. Data: [researchers.json](https://www.dysnet.org/data/researchers.json)
- [Care centres](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/care-centres/): 95 centres of care, each named by a member association or verified on its own institutional page. Data: [care-centres.json](https://www.dysnet.org/data/care-centres.json)
- [Teratogens](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/teratogens/): 577 substances with known, presumed or suspected effects on the unborn child, with evidence level and legal status. Data: [teratogens.json](https://www.dysnet.org/data/teratogens.json)

## Reference pages

- [Understanding dysmelia](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/understanding-dysmelia/): what dysmelia is, condition by condition, with ORPHAcodes, ICD-10 and ICD-11 codes and the Oberg-Manske-Tonkin group. Data: [orphanet-hierarchy.json](https://www.dysnet.org/data/orphanet-hierarchy.json), where each code sits in Orphanet's classification.
- [Epidemiology](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/epidemiology/): birth prevalence per condition with its source and confidence interval, and expected affected births a year for 217 countries. Data: [births.json](https://www.dysnet.org/data/births.json), [condition-prevalence.json](https://www.dysnet.org/data/condition-prevalence.json)
- [Causes of dysmelia](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/causes-of-dysmelia/): a referenced review of what is known about causes, and how often a cause is found.
- [What is a patient-owned registry?](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/guides/patient-owned-registry/): the guide in two minutes.
- [The registry project](https://www.dysnet.org/registry/): the registry DysNet is building, and how it is governed.
- [Our voice](https://www.dysnet.org/voice/): DysNet's seats at EURORDIS, the European Disability Forum and ERN BOND.
- [Member associations](https://www.dysnet.org/about/members/): the associations families belong to, country by country.

## Filtered views can be linked

- Bibliography by condition: https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/bibliography/?condition=2911 (ORPHAcode), by theme: ?topic=meta, by year: ?from=2015&to=2026
- Teratogens by source, level, kind or use: https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/teratogens/?source=clp&level=known
- Expected affected births by condition and region: https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/epidemiology/?condition=amelia-all-forms&region=Sub-Saharan%20Africa

## The registry's technical partner

- [Health Data Safe](https://www.healthdatasafe.org/en/): a Swiss non-profit foundation that builds open-source infrastructure for people to gather, read and share their own health data, for their care and for research. By decision of DysNet's Annual General Meeting of 26 August 2026 it is the registry's technical and operational partner, contributing its infrastructure in kind. Wikidata: [Q141112222](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q141112222).
- How the two fit together: https://www.dysnet.org/registry/?for=registries explains the interoperability and portability offered to other registries; every person holds their own data account and nothing is pooled without a granular, revocable consent.

## Every other page

- [About DysNet](https://www.dysnet.org/about/): DysNet, formerly EDRIC: the network for people with congenital limb differences, founded by thalidomide families and registered in Sweden in 2009.
- [Statutes](https://www.dysnet.org/about/statutes/): The statutes of DYSNET (EDRIC), adopted 20 October 2011: objective, membership, meetings, board, accounts and amendment rules, readable online.
- [Transparency](https://www.dysnet.org/about/transparency/): DysNet's governing documents in one place: statutes, annual accounts, AGM documents and reports, published for members and the public.
- [Accessibility](https://www.dysnet.org/accessibility/): How accessible this site is, measured rather than claimed: what we tested, what passed, where it still falls short, and how to tell us when something blocks you.
- [Contact](https://www.dysnet.org/contact/): Contact DysNet: info@dysnet.org, offices in Solna (Sweden) and Brussels (Belgium). For families, clinicians, researchers and associations.
- [Support DysNet](https://www.dysnet.org/donate/): A one-off or monthly gift, membership or help in kind carries the three missions families rely on: knowledge, the registry and our voice.
- [Knowledge](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/): Five maintained registers on limb difference: bibliography, registries, researchers, care centres and teratogens, plus studies you can join.
- [Studies](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/ongoing-studies/): Limb-difference studies recruiting or under way: the ERN BOND Patient Journey, the Rare Barometer, prosthesis reimbursement, and who to contact.
- [Resources](https://www.dysnet.org/knowledge/resources/): Guides, surveys and reports on dysmelia that are not research papers: Orphanet sheets, the Rare Barometer, European registry recommendations.
- [Privacy](https://www.dysnet.org/privacy/): DysNet asks once whether it may count your visit, and collects nothing else through this site. What is processed, what the registers name, and your rights under the GDPR.
- [Reports](https://www.dysnet.org/voice/reports/): Short written reports from DysNet's delegates after every meeting in the bodies where DysNet represents families affected by limb difference.
